text:
git -c commit.gpgsign=false commit -q -F - <<'MSG'
fix(preg): preg_match() wrote `true` into $matches, or filled an array nothing could read

Two failures, and between them all three ways of writing the idiom were wrong.

An UNDECLARED `$matches` was created the way every out-parameter is — a boxed
null cell — and handed to a callee that does not replace the caller's slot at
all: `preg_match` FILLS the array it is given, in place. The runtime wrote
through that cell as though it were an array, and `var_dump($matches)` answered
`bool(true)` where php answers a three-element array. `count($matches)` on the
same variable was an uncaught TypeError.

Declaring `$matches = []` first got past that, and into the second one: the
lowering keeps its own local-type map, and nothing widened it after the call, so
it still believed `array<never>`. `count($m)` said 3 while every `$m[$i]` and
every `foreach` value read NULL — right and wrong out of one variable, in
silence. Only `$m = ["x"]`, already `array<string>`, read back correctly.

MEASURED on `php -n` 8.5.6: all three answer `["b", "", "b"]`, and an unmatched
optional group is the EMPTY STRING, not a gap.

The type is one answer both layers now read. The checker had it inline and the
lowering had none; a second copy would be a second thing to forget. Its test
asserts the parameter the entry names is still the one the CONTRACT marks
by-reference with an empty-array default, so the shape this module states and
the facts the registry states cannot drift apart.

Found because the smoke suite's own `preg_match_captures` had been failing while
saying only "IR backend binary failed" — the harness now prints what the binary
printed, which is how the TypeError became visible at all.
